stories.headline: Trumbull police car-seat check Saturday at Nichols Firehouse
stories.summary: Trumbull police will host a rain-or-shine car seat safety check Saturday, September 26, from 10 a.m. to noon at Nichols Firehouse, 582 Booth Hill Road. Certified child passenger safety technicians will help with car-seat and booster installation and inspection. The department’s message is simple: keep kids safe on every ride, every time.

stories.headline: 6th Circuit greenlights Ohio proof-of-citizenship law for midterms
stories.summary: A 2–1 Sixth Circuit panel stayed a district court injunction, letting Ohio enforce documentary proof-of-citizenship when voters register through the Bureau of Motor Vehicles ahead of the midterms. Trump-appointed Judges Nalbandian and Hermandorfer cited standing, mootness, and Purcell concerns; Biden appointee Judge Ritz dissented. Election-integrity groups backed the stay as the Oct. 5 registration deadline approaches.

stories.headline: Trump admin will ask Supreme Court to revive third-country deportations
stories.summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department will immediately seek Supreme Court relief after a First Circuit order blocked rapid third-country removals. The appeals court put into effect a ruling that migrants must get meaningful notice and a chance to raise persecution or torture fears before being sent to countries other than their own. Officials say more than 25,000 migrants have been sent to at least 29 third countries under the policy.

stories.headline: Apple shares new video promoting iOS 27 parental controls
stories.summary: Apple released a video highlighting iOS 27 child-safety tools: easier Child Account setup, Ask to Buy, Ask to Browse for Safari, Communication Safety that can block violence and nudity in Messages and FaceTime, and Time Allowances with one-tap pause for family events. The features shipped September 14 with iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS Golden Gate, and every device in a Family Sharing group needs the latest software for Screen Time updates to work.

stories.headline: Beats 360 headphones hit Apple Stores, Best Buy, and Target shelves
stories.summary: Beats 360 over-ear headphones are available in many Apple Stores worldwide today, with some Best Buy and Target stock as well. Priced at $349.99, they offer stronger noise cancellation than Studio Pro, Personalized Spatial Audio, Transparency mode, Adaptive EQ, and IPX4 sweat resistance, plus swappable Performance Knit and UltraPlush cushions. Add-on cushions are $9.99 through October 31.

stories.headline: Penguins’ Andrei Kuzmenko takes leave after father dies in Siberia bear attack
stories.summary: Forward Andrei Kuzmenko practiced with Pittsburgh on Thursday morning, then left for Moscow after learning his father, Alexander, 62, was killed by a bear on a fishing trip in southern Siberia’s Tuva Republic. GM Kyle Dubas asked for privacy and said the family has the organization’s full support; coach Dan Muse offered condolences. Kuzmenko signed a one-year, $5 million deal with the Penguins on July 1.

stories.headline: Geno Smith: Jets still turnover-free entering Lions Week 3
stories.summary: Geno Smith says protecting the ball remains the emphasis as the Jets enter Week 3 at Detroit still without a turnover — only the second such start in franchise history and the first in 55 years. Aaron Glenn wants more explosive downfield shots after a wet Packers loss; Detroit has allowed six passing touchdowns already. Smith trusts the process and the chemistry building with Frank Reich’s offense.

stories.headline: Starship Flight 14 wet dress under way; orbital window opens Monday
stories.summary: With Ship 41 stacked on Super Heavy Booster 21 at Starbase Pad 2, SpaceX ran opportunistic full-stack wet-dress testing Thursday ahead of Flight 14 — Starship’s first orbital attempt. A 75-minute window opens 8:15 a.m. EDT Monday, September 28, pending regulatory approval. The ~10-hour mission would deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites and target Pacific splashdowns after about six orbits.

stories.headline: LEGO Ideas Wallace & Gromit (21371): 1,038 pieces, $99.99, Oct. 1
stories.summary: LEGO Ideas set 21371 brings Wallace and Gromit to bricks for the first time: 1,038 pieces, ages 18+, $99.99 / £89.99, available October 1. The build recreates the Close Shave motorbike and sidecar with poseable figures and accessories such as crackers, wool, and a diamond in the seat hatch. It grew from Fan Designer Pidelium’s winning LEGO Ideas “90s Throwback” challenge entry.

stories.headline: CT peak foliage forecast later — and more vibrant — this fall
stories.summary: UConn Extension’s Thomas Worthley expects Connecticut’s peak foliage in mid- to late October — later than usual — as warm temperatures and a very wet summer keep trees greener longer. Bridgeport’s June–August rainfall topped 21 inches. Less maple fungal browning should mean richer reds, yellows, and oranges; DEEP maps peak roughly Oct. 14–20 north, Oct. 21–27 central, and Oct. 28–Nov. 3 south.

stories.headline: GAO: ICE wasted tens of millions on rushed detention expansion plans
stories.summary: A Government Accountability Office report says ICE and partner agencies wasted tens of millions chasing ill-conceived detention projects after Trump ordered mass arrests — including nearly $3 million for unused Guantánamo tents and $20 million tied to warehouses bought then left empty. Congress gave ICE $45 billion to expand capacity, but investigators say the agency still lacks a strategic spending plan. DHS told GAO a plan may not arrive until August 2027.
